title: Pelliot chinois 2449
shelf_note: A Chinese manuscript fragment (Pelliot chinois, Dunhuang) in red ink. Its vocabulary (天尊 as I read it, 天王, 龍神, 皇祠) fits the catalogued Daoist scripture. No tradition or collections are set, so there is nothing to contradict.
structure_note: The structure count gives pages_translated 0, but the book's pages_translated field is 14, and this page does carry a translation. The counts disagree with each other. The single 'printed number' is the pencil shelfmark 2449, which the OCR tagged as <page-num>; it is not a page number.

pages.printed_marker: 2449 v° (pencil archival/shelf number at top; reading of the small suffix uncertain)
pages.layout: two vertical columns of red-ink running script at the right edge of an octagonally trimmed, stained fragment; the rest of the leaf is blank

ocr_errors.image: 天尊帝輦来儀 (one character, apparently 尊, between 天 and 帝)
ocr_errors.problem: One character is read as two ('南皇'), which turns 'the Celestial Worthy's imperial carriage' into a 'Heavenly South' emperor. The OCR meta's Vietnamese attribution and the translation's opening both grow out of this misreading.

ocr_errors.image: 龍神助讃嘆 (speech radical; 讃嘆 'praise')
ocr_errors.problem: 讃 misread as 清, so the translation has 'clear sighs'

ocr_errors.image: 豈而宜?真?助以斯景福 (a character is dropped before 助; 斯 not 此)
ocr_errors.problem: One character is omitted and 斯 is read as 此; I am unsure of the cursive at the head of the column

ocr_errors.image: 津狼 (犭 + 良), probably standing for 津梁 'ford-bridge'
ocr_errors.problem: misread as 狽, which yields the 'ford of hardship' rendering
室 ('hall, chamber') read as 至, so 'the whole hall' is lost
The archival number is tagged as a page number

tr_errors.english: In the Heavenly South <note>original: "天南"; literally "south of heaven," a poetic name for a southern realm</note>, the Emperor's carriage comes with fitting ceremony.
tr_errors.problem: The note gives confident learning (a southern realm) to a misread. The image appears to read 天尊帝輦, the Celestial Worthy's imperial carriage.

tr_errors.english: let there be no limit; do not depend on the <unclear>ford of hardship</unclear>
tr_errors.problem: 莫限 ('without limit') is split into two clauses, and the verb 'do not depend on' is invented to make a clause for 津狽

tr_errors.english: Clear sighs of praise rise in the air
tr_errors.problem: 'Clear' comes from the misread 清 (the image has 讃 'praise')

other.note: The OCR <meta> asserts 'likely of Vietnamese Hán-Nôm origin given the opening phrase "Thiên Nam"'. This is an invented provenance claim, built on a misread, for a Pelliot Dunhuang manuscript.

The translation <meta> claims 'This page overlaps closely with the closing lines of the previous page's translation and appears to be a fuller witness of the same passage'. The page cannot support this continuity claim.

original: "天王"; in Buddhist usage, the guardian kings of th
original: "龍神"; protective serpent or dragon deities in Bud
original: "景福"; a stock phrase for abundant good fortune
original: "津狽"; the reading and sense are uncertain
original: "庄嚴" (zhuangyan); the Buddhist term for adorning
original: "皇祠"; an ancestral or imperial hall of worship

missing.english: the Emperor's carriage comes with fitting ceremony
missing.why: The reader is not told which emperor or deity is meant. In this Daoist scripture it is most likely the Celestial Worthy (天尊), and nothing says so.

book_verdict: The page is the right leaf, but the cursive red-ink OCR misreads a key character (天尊 as 天南皇). That misreading feeds an invented Vietnamese-origin claim in the meta and a footnoted 'Heavenly South' opening, so an expert would flag the page on sight.
